output.name: Sathun

anatomy.part: belly of the jar, the water kept inside
lid peg on top of the lid
inner edge of the handle loop
outer top of the handle loop
left wall where the rope crosses the jar
far end of the tie-down rope

output.myth: When Aun cut the string he left the houses without their water, and the Gulls came down to the cliffs in the dry months to drink from anyone's jar. Mother Hesk, who keeps count of everything, said nothing. She only tied the lids. So the people of the cliffs learned to tie the lid down with rope, and to keep the jar near the hearth where the smoke can reach it. Ennu made the first one from fired clay and a bone peg, and the Gulls still come to the cliff edge, look, and go away hungry. Tavo once lifted a jar off a roof and laughed, and the rope held, and that is why we double the knots. A jar is a small sky: closed, full, and still on the earth. The bright one at its belly is the water we have kept, and the peg is the knot that holds it.
output.verse:
Lid tied down with rope,
the Gulls can't get the water,
dry months, sweet and cold.
